Study Layout

Experience

Lesson Goal

Use simple English when transport changes. Ask again, check the exit or stop, ask for card help, and make a calm backup plan.

Introduction

This lesson continues Risa's transport practice. In the first transport lesson, Risa asked for the right line, bought a ticket, checked the platform, took a bus, and asked for directions.

Key Idea

This time, the transport is still simple, but small problems happen. A platform changes.

Risa cannot find the right exit. Her card does not work at the gate.

A bus driver speaks quickly. She misses one stop.

The goal is to stay calm and ask one short question again.

Main Question

Good travel English is not perfect English. It is useful English.

Risa uses short sentences, repeats important words, and shows her phone when speaking is hard.

Warm-Up Questions

  • Do you feel nervous at a busy station?
  • What do you check before you get on a train or bus?
  • What can you say when you are not sure?
  • What can you do if you miss your stop?

Final Reflection

Transport problems often feel big, but the English can stay small. Check the platform again.

Ask for the right exit. Ask for help when a card or ticket does not work.

Check the bus before you get on. If you miss a stop, ask, "What should I do?"

Key Point

Risa does not need long English. She needs calm English.

Her best tools are short questions, repeating the answer, showing her phone, and making one backup plan.

Final Speaking Task

Useful Speaking Patterns

  • Excuse me. Is this correct?
  • Which platform for ...?
  • Which exit for ...?
  • My card is not working.
  • Do I need to add money?
  • Does this bus go near ...?
  • Where should I get off?
  • I missed my stop.
  • What should I do?
  • Is it safe to walk?
  • Is there a taxi stand near here?
  • I have a backup plan now.

Practice Questions

  • Which problem is most stressful for you: platform change, wrong exit, card problem, bus stop, or rain?
  • What phrase from this lesson do you want to remember first?
  • When should you show your phone?
  • What is your backup plan if you miss a train or bus?
  • What can you repeat to check the answer?
  • Practice a role-play with a teacher. First use Risa's lines. Then change one detail: the place, platform, exit, stop, or problem.
